The helper then reports that git lacks the 'preparing' state, and the forced-race control is always skipped, even on Apple Git >= 2.48.

Section 'Git version floor gate' in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml enforces only git >= 2.38, so CI or dev hosts on git 2.38-2.47 pass the gate but skip this control.
The plan's Testing section says 'pytest ... passes' and doesn't say which git version it ran under. On older git, 'passes' can just mean 'skipped'.
findings.finding: The plan says the root cause is confirmed with a deterministic reproduction and that the test's verdict no longer depends on host load. But the forced race needs git's `preparing` reference-transaction state, which the code says arrived in Git 2.48. On any older git the test skips and never gives a verdict. The repo supports Git from 2.38 and its stated rule is to fail with an upgrade message, not skip. The plan doesn't mention this dependency, and the 2.48 version claim in the code is unverified.
scenarios: A developer or CI runner on git 2.40-2.47 runs make verify. The positive control skips silently, so a regression in is_ref_cas_mismatch or in the CAS signature it matches would go unnoticed.

The 'preparing' state turns out to have been added in a different git release than 2.48, so the skip threshold is wrong: either the test skips needlessly or it runs where the hook never fires and fails.

findings.finding: Fitness for purpose: the new forced control checks a stand-in property. It shows that a ref moved between read and lock yields a message is_ref_cas_mismatch recognises. It no longer shows that uncoordinated fetches sharing one common dir race, and it never exercises the coordination path. The coordinated negative test (test_coordination_prevents_the_cas_race) still asserts zero races under real scheduling. That test drew its discriminating power from the original positive control showing the same workload races without the lock. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin hook discovery for the forced-race fetch: pass `-c core.hooksPath=<common-dir>/hooks` (or set it in the worktree's local config) so ambient global/system git config cannot bypass the hook.
evidence: Verified: tests/_subprocess_env.py:35-37 copies os.environ unchanged, and nothing isolates GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM for this fetch
docs/local-dev-env.md:189-193: '`core.hooksPath` snag ... it may be set **globally**'
Makefile:121-142 has dedicated handling for a globally set core.hooksPath
Other tests set the hook path explicitly, e.g. tests/unit/test_push_pending_marker.py:81 `config core.hooksPath <origin>/hooks`
Plan § Testing only reports runs on the author's host and does not state a hook-discovery precondition
findings.finding: The force-race hook is written to `<common-git-dir>/hooks/reference-transaction`, but git only reads that directory when `core.hooksPath` is unset. The fetch inherits the ambient environment through `subprocess_env(...)`, including global and system git config. On a host where `core.hooksPath` is set globally, which this repo's own docs and Makefile call a common snag, the hook never runs. The fetch then succeeds and the positive control fails every time. The verdict would depend on the host's git config instead of host load.
scenarios: A developer with a global `core.hooksPath` (a pre-commit or husky-style setup) runs make verify, the hook is skipped, and the test fails with a non-CAS output
A CI image's system gitconfig sets core.hooksPath
findings.suggested_fix: In the test, run `git -C <wt> -c core.hooksPath=<common_git_dir>/hooks fetch ...`. Alternatively, run the fetch with `subprocess_env(REBAR_FORCE_CAS_RACE='1', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1')`, which follows the pattern in tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py:27.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the git >= 2.48 (`preparing` hook state) precondition in the plan, confirm it against git's release notes or `git help hooks`, and parse the version robustly (regex `git version (\d+)\.(\d+)`) so vendor suffixes don't cause false skips.
evidence: Code: `raw = out.stdout.split()[-1]`; `parts = tuple(int(p) for p in raw.split('.')[:2] if p.isdigit())`; `return parts < (2, 48)`
Partially-verified: the docstring says 'Git added the `preparing` reference-transaction state in 2.48'. I could not confirm this against git release notes or `git help hooks` here
Absence: the plan § Testing and the ACs never mention the git-version dependency or the skip path
findings.finding: The plan doesn't mention the new external-capability precondition: the `preparing` reference-transaction state requires git >= 2.48. The version gate also decides silently to skip, and its parsing is fragile. `out.stdout.split()[-1]` takes the last token. For vendor strings such as `git version 2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)` that token is `Git-154)`, which yields an empty tuple, and `() < (2, 48)` is True, so the test skips even when the version is new enough. When the test skips, the positive control is gone without any failure, so the AC's 'deterministic reproduction' holds only on hosts whose `git --version` is plain and >= 2.48.
scenarios: macOS Apple Git: the suffix makes the parse return () and the control always skips
A CI or developer host with git < 2.48 skips without any failure, so the CAS signature recogniser `is_ref_cas_mismatch` is never exercised there
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the parse with `m = re.search(r'git version (\d+)\.(\d+)', out.stdout); return m is None or (int(m[1]), int(m[2])) < (2, 48)`. Add a line to § Testing naming the minimum git version and the git version used for the 5/5 runs.
